info.name: Flowty
info.description: Health, auth, boards (ownership + membership + invitations), tasks (owner/assignee permissions), users, and activity endpoints for the Flowty backend. Import this directly into Postman. Run folders top-to-bottom: Auth -> Boards -> Board Members & Invitations -> Tasks -> Users -> Activity -> Cleanup — each folder's happy-path requests save the collection variables the next folder needs, and Cleanup removes the test invitee from the board at the end so the whole run is repeatable.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Run 'Register' first — it saves {{token}} and {{userId}} (the board owner's account) for every folder below, and doubles as the setup step 'Register (duplicate email)' depends on. Re-running the whole collection against the same database will fail at 'Register' with a real 409 (the account already exists) — either run 'Login' instead to refresh {{token}}/{{userId}}, or use a fresh database.

item.name: Boards

exec: console.log('boardId + columns saved:', json.id, json.columns[0].id, json.columns[1].id);

item.name: Create board (scratch, for the delete test below)

item.description: 'Create board' saves {{boardId}}, {{columnId}}, and {{columnId2}} (its first two default columns, 'To Do' and 'Doing') for the folders below — that board is kept around for the rest of the collection. The delete test uses a separate disposable 'scratch' board instead, so deleting it doesn't break {{boardId}} references in every other folder. The 'not the owner' negative test for boards lives in 'Board Members & Invitations' instead of here, since it needs {{inviteeToken}}, which doesn't exist until that folder runs.

item.name: Board Members & Invitations
List members (owner + invitee not yet on it)
List board's pending invitations (not owner — expect 403)
Respond to invitation (not addressed to me — expect 403)
Respond to invitation again (already responded — expect 409)

item.description: Run 'Register invitee' once (or 'Login as invitee' on later runs, since the account persists) to get {{inviteeEmail}}/{{inviteeToken}}/{{inviteeUserId}}, then run the rest top-to-bottom. 'Invite member by email' saves {{invitationId}}. The invitee is left as an active member here on purpose — the Tasks folder assigns them a task to test the assignee-only permissions — and only gets removed by the 'Cleanup' folder at the very end.

item.name: Tasks
Create task (not the board owner — expect 403)
Update task (assignee moves it to another column — allowed)
Update task (assignee tries to edit the title — expect 403)
Delete task (assignee, not the owner — expect 403)

item.description: Run after 'Board Members & Invitations', which leaves {{inviteeUserId}} as an actual member of {{boardId}} — this folder assigns the task straight to them so the assignee-only permission checks (move allowed, edit rejected) are testing something real, not just the owner's own full access. Uses {{columnId}}/{{columnId2}} (the board's first two default columns, 'To Do' and 'Doing') from the Boards folder. 'Create task' saves {{taskId}}/{{taskVersion}}; each successful update refreshes {{taskVersion}} for the next request.

item.name: Cleanup
item.description: Removes the invitee from the board once every folder above that needed them as a member has run, so 'Board Members & Invitations' → 'Invite member by email' can be re-run from a clean slate without hitting the 'already a member' conflict.
